חֵרֶם m. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding)
1) net. Kelim XXIII, 5; XXVIII, 9, see זֶוֶט; and from—Nedarim II, 5, see infra.

—2) a place adapted for catching fish in nets, fishing coast, fishery. Bava Kamma 81ᵇ מלא חבל ח׳ בדרומה a rope’s length (district) of fishing coast south of it (the Lake of Tiberias); Tosefta ib. VIII, 18 Variant ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta)—Eruvin 47ᵇ ח׳ שבין וכ׳ a fishpond between two territories.

—3) [cut off, excluded, compare חוּלִּין, הֶפְקֵר,] ḥerem, property set apart for priest’s or Temple use; doomed to destruction. Nedarim II, 4 אם כח׳ של שמים if (he said, This shall be to me) like the ḥerem consecrated to the Temple, opposed ח׳ של כהנים assigned to the private use of priests. Ib. 5 נדר בח׳ … בחֶרְמוֹ של ים if he made a vow of abstinence using the word ḥerem, and he says, I meant the ḥerem of the sea (fisher’s net). Ib. I, 2 כינויין לח׳ verbal substitutes for ḥerem (effecting prohibition); and from

—4) excommunication. Moʿed Katan 17ᵃ.—plural חֲרָמִים, חֲרָמִין. Sanhedrin 43ᵇ מעל עכן בג׳ ח׳ Akhan committed three sacrileges. Nedarim II, 4 סתם ח׳ containing the expression ḥerem unqualified. Ib. חַרְמֵי הכהנים the dedications as priestly property. Arakhin VIII, 6 סתם ח׳ לבדק הבית unqualified dedications (this be ḥerem) go to the repair of the Temple; and from—[Yerushalmi Kilayim IX, 32ᵃ top שצבעה בחרם, read: בחֶרֶת.]—V. חֵירוּם.

חָלוּק I m. (חָלַק, see חָלָק) plain, smooth garment, in gen. undershirt. Kelim XXVIII, 9, see חוּץ II.—Moʿed Katan 14ᵃ, and e. כל … אלא ח׳ אחד he who has only one shirt. Pirkei Avot Zar. 34ᵃ ח׳ לבן a plain white frock, see אִימְּרָה. Yerushalmi Taanit II, 65ᵈ (reference. to I Samuel VII, 6) לבש שמואל חֲלוּקָן וכ׳ Samuel put on the common shirt of all Israelites, i.e. included himself among the sinners; and from—Transferred a) a shirt-shaped bandage. Shabbat XIX, 2 (drawn over the circumcised membrum).—b) a row, layer. Yerushalmi Pesachim I, 27ᵇ bottom of page מפשיטו ח׳ אחד he strips it of one shirt, i.e. removes one row all around the pile of bottles.—plural חֲלוּקִים, חֲלוּקִין, חֲלוּקוֹת. Moʿed Katan 22ᵇ. Yerushalmi l. common gender. שני חלקות (read: חלוק׳) two rows. Tosefta Kilayim V, 6 שני ח׳ two shirts of different materials (כִּלְאַיִם). Eicha Rabbah introduction (R. Abbahu 2); ib. to III, 13 והח׳ שלו עליו (the camel) with his covers on; and from

חוּץ II m. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding)
1) that which is divided off, outside, street. Kelim XXVIII, 9 חלוק של יוצאת הח׳ the shirt of the runabout (prostitute; see Smith, Dictionary of Greek and Roman Antiquities, Third American Edition, New-York 1858 section (Parashah) see Coa Vestis and Diaphane Heimata; Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra V, 14 יוצאות החוט going out of the line of custom). Zevachim 57ᵇ; Yoma 57ᵃ ח׳ ופנים Arukh (see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l note 2, and Tosafot to Zevachim l. common gender.) what is done outside the Temple and what inside. Chullin VI, 2 השוחט … בח׳ he who slaughters unconsecrated animals within the Temple court, or consecrated animals without. Ib. 85ᵃ שחוטי ח׳ consecrated animals slaughtered outside the Temple court. Ib. 68ᵃ וצתה ח׳ למחיצתו was carried outside of its legal limits; and from—בַּח׳, מִבַּח׳ outside, from outside, לַח׳ out (through the window &c.). Shabbat I, 1. Pirkei Avot Zar. 11ᵃ; and see from

—2) (followed by מ־) except, without. Chullin I, 1 ח׳ מחרש וכ׳ except a deaf and dumb &c. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 49 ח׳ מדעתו without consulting him; and see from
יוֹצֵאת f. constr., י׳ החוץ (preceding) running about, prostitute. Kelim XXVIII, 9; Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra V, 14, see חוּץ II.—plural יוֹצְאוֹת. Ib. some ed.

לְסוֹטָה (subaudi בגד, חלוק) m. (orig. = לַסּוֹטָה, used as an independent word as if from a root לסט, compare לָמַס) the thin web worn by loose women (= חלוק של יוצאת החוץ, Kelim XXVIII, 9, see חוּץ II); in gen. fine veil. Yerushalmi Shabbat VI, 8ᵇ bottom of page (explained רדידים, Isaiah III, 23) ל׳ כמה דתימר וכ׳ it is the dress of the ill-reputed, as we read (Song of Songs V, 7) they took my veil &c. (believing her to be a harlot). Ib. XIII, beginning, 14ᵃ וההן ל׳ אפי׳ בסוף וכ׳ (not לסיטה) as regards the thin web, even the finishing (adding the fringe) is considered an act of weaving (in the Sabbath law). Yerushalmi Moʿed Katan II, 81ᵇ top הורון בהדין ל׳ וכ׳ decided concerning (the sale of) stuff for veils (during the festive week) &c.—plural לְסוֹטוֹת. Yerushalmi Shabbat IV, 7ᵃ top, see חָף.—Chald. form: לְסוֹטַיָּיא. Yerushalmi Bava Metzia IV, end, 9ᵈ ר׳ … הוה עסיק בל׳ R. A. was engaged in weaving veils. Ib. מנן באילין ל׳ what dare we do with those veils (dare we use means to give them a fine appearance)?

סְבָכָה, שְׂ׳ f. (Biblical Hebrew שְׂ׳) 1) same.)
1) same. Tosefta Shabbat IV (V), 11 ס׳ המוזהבת (ed. Lag. סבכא, Variant ספכא, correct accordingly) a gold-embroidered hair net; Shabbat 57ᵇ. Yerushalmi ib. VI, 8ᵇ bottom of page; Negaim XI, 11, and from שביס של ס׳, see שָׁבִיס; Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra V, 15 שביס של ש׳. Shabbat l. common gender. כל שהוא למטה מן הש׳ whatever ornament is worn beneath the net; ib. 65ᵃ הס׳; (Tosefta ib. IV (V), 7 חיפוי שלמטה משערה); and from

—2) any net-work, mat &c. Kelim XXVIII, 9 ס׳ של זקנה the old woman’s net-work (mat to sit upon, see Maimonides and l.). Ib. חלוק … העשוי כס׳ the public woman’s shirt which is like net-work (gauze, see חוּץ II). Yerushalmi Terumot VIII, 45ᵈ אירס … עומד כס׳ the venom of the serpent remains on top (of liquids) as a net-like film; Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. II, 41ᵈ top דומה לש׳; Yerushalmi Shabbat I, 3ᵈ top עשוי כש׳; and from—Ib. VI, 7ᵈ טבוסה, read שבכה, see כָּבוּל II.—plural סְבָכוֹת, שְׂ׳. Kelim XXIV, 16; Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra II, 10 שלש ס׳ הן וכ׳ there are three categories of nets with regard to levitical cleanness; and e.

סַבָּל m. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding) load-carrier. Yerushalmi Bava Metzia X, end, 12ᶜ; (Bavli ib. 118ᵇ כַּתָּף). Kiddushin 82ᵇ; Yerushalmi ib. IV, end, 66ᵈ; Tosefta ib. V, 15 (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) note). Midrash Tanḥuma, ed. Bub., M’tsora 11 בריאים כסַבָּלוֹ של עולם as strong as he who carries the world; Yalkut Psalms 808.—plural סַבָּלִין. Kelim XXVIII, 9 כסת הס׳ the cushion which load-carriers wear on their heads.

צְפִירָא II, צְפִירָה I f. (preceding) she-goat; goat’s hair, shag. Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra II, 11 של צפירא (sandals) of goat’s hair. Ib. V, 12 של צפורה (Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim XXVIII, 9 צפירה) (a strainer) of goat’s hair. Ib. IV, 14 של צפור ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (correct accordingly) mats of goat’s hair; Sukkah 20ᵇ של סְפִירָא of (loosely woven) shag (see Rashi in Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 200); [Rashi, from ספר to shear: horse-hair from the mane or the tail].

sections.en: A porter's pad is susceptible to midras uncleanness. A wine filter is not susceptible to uncleanness as a seat. An old woman's hair-net is susceptible to uncleanness as a seat. A prostitute's shirt which is woven like a net is not susceptible to uncleanness. A garment made of fishing net is not susceptible to uncleanness, but one made of its bag is susceptible. Rabbi Eliezer ben Jacob says: if a garment is made out of a fishing net but is made double it is susceptible to uncleanness.
sections.he: כֶּסֶת הַסַּבָּלִין, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס. מְשַׁמֶּרֶת שֶׁל יַיִן, אֵין בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם מוֹשָׁב. סְבָכָה שֶׁל זְקֵנָה, טְמֵאָה מִשּׁוּם מוֹשָׁב. חָלוּק שֶׁל יוֹצֵאת הַחוּץ הֶעָשׂוּי כִּסְבָכָה, טָהוֹר. הָעוֹשֶׂה בֶגֶד מִן הַחֵרֶם, טָהוֹר. וּמִזּוּטוֹ, טָמֵא. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, אַף הָעוֹשֶׂה בֶגֶד מִן הַחֵרֶם וּכְפָלוֹ, טָמֵא:

en: קַרְקָרָה f. (compare קַרְקַע) rimmed bottom of a vessel; lower border of a web. Oholot IX, 16 כנגד קַרְקָרָתָהּ ed. Dehr. and Arukh ed. Kohelet (ed. קוּרְקוּרוּתָהּ, קוּרְקְרוּתָהּ) corresponding to (under or on the rim of) its bottom; Tosefta ib. X, 9 קורקורתיה ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (read קוּרְקוּרְתָּהּ or קוּרְקְרוֹתֶיהָ); ib. קוּרְקַרְתָּהּ, קוּרְקוּרְתָּהּ. Kelim XXVIII, 10 עד שיגמור את קַרְקַרְתָּהּ ed. Dehr. (ed. קורקורתה; Arukh קוּרְקְרוֹתֶיהָ, ed. Kohelet קר׳ plural) until he finishes the lower border of the network.—plural קַרְקָרוֹת. Ib. II, 2 קַרְקְרוֹתֵיהֶן. Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma II, 2 קרקרנות (correct accordingly; Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim II, 2 תוך). Ib. VII, 15 קַרְקְעוֹת הכלים the bottoms of vessels.

שָׁבִיס m. (Biblical Hebrew; שבס, compare שָׁבַשׁ; compare Biblical Hebrew שְׂרוֹךְ and שָׂרַךְ) band, especially (של סבכה) ש׳ metal (or woolen) band with which the hair-net is fastened. Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra V, 15 ש׳ של שבכה טמא וכ׳ a net-band is susceptible of uncleanness for itself, because one may (detach and) fit it for another net. Ib. 16 ומשום חיבורי ש׳ וכ׳ but (gold foils and plates) used as fastenings of a hair-band are susceptible of uncleanness. Kelim XXVIII, 10 ש׳ שלה the band of the net. Negaim XI, 11. Sifra Sh’mini, Chaldaic VII, Parah 8 שָׁבִיץ של סבכה; ib. Chaldaic XI, Parah 10 שביס וכ׳ a woolen net-band. Yerushalmi Shabbat VI, 8ᵇ bottom of page (reference. to שביסים, Isaiah III, 18) braided bands (see סִלְבּוֹנַיָּא) כמה דאת אמר ש׳ של סבכה as you say, shabis of the hair-net.

sections.en: A hair-net that one began to make from its upper hem remains pure until its bottom section is finished. If one began from its bottom section, it remains pure until its hem is finished. Its head band is susceptible to uncleanness in itself. Its strings are susceptible to uncleanness because they are connected. A hair-net that is torn becomes pure if it cannot contain the greater part of the hair.
sections.he: סְבָכָה שֶׁהִתְחִיל בָּהּ מִפִּיהָ, טְהוֹרָה, עַד שֶׁיִּגְמֹר אֶת קוּרְקוּרְתָּהּ. הִתְחִיל בָּהּ מִקּוּרְקוּרְתָּהּ, טְהוֹרָה, עַד שֶׁיִּגְמֹר אֶת פִּיהָ. שָׁבִיס שֶׁלָּהּ, טָמֵא בִפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ. הַחוּטִין שֶׁלָּהּ, טְמֵאִין מִשּׁוּם חִבּוּר. סְבָכָה שֶׁנִּקְרְעָה, אִם אֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת אֶת רֹב הַשֵּׂעָר, טְהוֹרָה:
